words.gloss: concerning knowledge of abnormal limbs/body parts

hindi: अब इसलिए हम विकृत अंगों के ज्ञान वाले अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on the knowledge of abnormal body parts (vikṛtāṅgavijñānīya).
notes: Standard chapter-opening formula. The chapter title is read as vikṛta-aṅga-vijñānīya, 'concerning the knowledge of abnormal limbs/parts of the body'; the adjective qualifies adhyāyam.

hindi: स्वस्थ या रोगी पुरुषों में, जो दूसरे शरीर की इच्छा करने वाले हैं, औषध की पहुँच से परे गए, पूरे शरीर में फैलने वाले दोष, बादल जैसे वर्षा को सूचित करते हैं वैसे ही आयु के क्षय को सूचित करते हुए, अचानक स्वभाव का विपर्यास उत्पन्न करते हैं।
english: The doṣas (humours) that have gone beyond the range of medicine and pervade the whole body, in men, whether healthy or afflicted, who desire another body, indicating the decay of life as clouds (indicate) rain, suddenly produce a reversal of natural state.

text_flags.why: possible: 'svasthanām' lacks the long ā of the genitive plural svasthānām; the split svastha-nām is also conceivable but gives no sense

notes: Elliptical comparison: 'ghanāghanā iva varṣam' takes its participle sūcayantaḥ from the next phrase (clouds indicating rain). ghanāghana is read as 'cloud'; other senses (dense, elephant) are not suitable here. The genitive plurals (of the healthy or afflicted men) are rendered 'in men'. dehāntarābhilāṣiṇām is literally 'desiring another body'; the text does not say 'dying'. Normalisation: viparyyāsa (doubled y) read viparyāsa.
lines_deva: स्वस्थनामातुराणां वा पुरुषाणां देहांतराभिलाषिणामौषधविषयमतीताःसकलशरीरव्यापिनो दोषा घनाघना इव वर्षमायुषः क्षयं सूचयंतोऽकस्मात्स्वभावविपर्य्यासं जनयंति
lines_iast: svasthanāmāturāṇāṃ vā puruṣāṇāṃ dehāṃtarābhilāṣiṇāmauṣadhaviṣayamatītāḥsakalaśarīravyāpino doṣā ghanāghanā iva varṣamāyuṣaḥ kṣayaṃ sūcayaṃto'kasmātsvabhāvaviparyyāsaṃ janayaṃti

hindi: उसे संक्षेप में रिष्ट यानी अनिष्ट सूचक लक्षण कहते हैं।
english: In brief, they call that riṣṭa (an ill-omen, a sign of approaching death).
notes: riṣṭa is a doctrinal term (a sign foretelling death); the gloss is a plain explanation, not a modern equivalent.

words.gloss: colours of the body's natural state

hindi: उनमें गौर या अगौर, श्याम या अश्याम, कृष्ण या अकृष्ण, ये देह की प्रकृति के वर्ण हैं।
english: Among these: fair or not fair, dusky or not dusky, black or not black: these are the colours of the body's natural state.
notes: The meaning of the a- forms is literal 'not fair' etc.; a sense 'slightly' (not very fair) is possible but not stated. 'or' is supplied to show the pairs; the text has none. prakṛti here is rendered 'natural state'. Reviewer: the printed Devanagari has a separate vowel इ (अकृष्ण इति written without a space), so there is no sandhi error and no typo; only the space is missing.
lines_deva: तत्र गौरोऽगौरः श्यामो ऽश्यामः कृष्णो ऽकृष्णइति देहप्रकृतिवर्णाः

words.gloss: lotus-fair and the like (padma = lotus, Nelumbo nucifera; standard)

hindi: और उनके भेद पद्मगौर यानी कमल के समान गौर आदि हैं।
english: And its varieties are lotus-fair (padmagaura) and the like.
notes: Verb understood (copula); none supplied beyond 'are'. padmagaura is read as 'fair like a lotus'; padma = lotus, Nelumbo nucifera (standard).

words.gloss: blue, dusky, copper-coloured, turmeric-yellow (haridrā, Curcuma longa; standard), white and the like
the natural-state colour and the abnormal colour

hindi: नील, श्याम, ताम्र, हारिद्र यानी हल्दी के रंग के, शुक्ल आदि तो विकृतियाँ हैं। उनमें प्रकृति का वर्ण और विकृति का वर्ण, छपाई बिगड़ी होने से अस्पष्ट शब्द के साथ या, मृत्यु के लिए होते हैं।
english: But blue, dusky, copper-coloured, turmeric-yellow, white and the like are abnormalities. Among these, the natural-state colour and the abnormal colour, unclear (damaged print: yugapadgaṃdhegaikadeśe, followed by vā 'or'), are for death.

text_flags.why: possible: 'gaṃdhega' is meaningless here; 'gātra-ekadeśe' (in one part of the body) fits the sense and the printed letters loosely (gā-tra / gaṃdhe-ga)
possible: extra t in 'śyāmat-tāmra'; read śyāma-tāmra

notes: The word 'yugapadgaṃdhegaikadeśe' is damaged and kept unsplit; the conjecture 'yugapad gātra-ekadeśe' (at once, or in one part of the body) stays in the flag and this note only; the translations say 'unclear' (glossary rule). 'vikṛtayaḥtatra' has a missing space (vikṛtayaḥ tatra). The verb is understood ('are'). maraṇāya is dative, 'for death', i.e. leading to death.
lines_deva: नीलश्यामत्ताम्रहारिद्रशुक्लादयस्तु विकृतयःतत्र प्रकृतिविकृतिवर्णौ युगपद्गंधेगैकदेशे वा मरणाय
lines_iast: nīlaśyāmattāmrahāridraśuklādayastu vikṛtayaḥtatra prakṛtivikṛtivarṇau yugapadgaṃdhegaikadeśe vā maraṇāya

words.gloss: fading, growth, grief, joy, dryness, unctuousness and the like
of those stated in the (passage) on varieties of prakṛti
by the division of doṣas etc.

hindi: इससे मुरझाना, अनुमानित पाठ पर वृद्धि, शोक, हर्ष, रूखापन, स्निग्धता आदि, तथा प्रकृतिभेदीय में कहे गए बड़े, उपचित, सूक्ष्म, दीर्घ, और दोष आदि के भाग से नियत सभी भावों का बिना कारण अन्यथा होना कहा गया है।
english: By this, the being otherwise without cause of fading, growth (on a conjectural reading), grief, joy, dryness, unctuousness and the like, and likewise of all the states stated in the (passage) on varieties of prakṛti (large, plump, fine, long) and determined by the division of doṣas etc., is stated.

text_flags.why: possible: 'uracaya' is not a word; 'upacaya' (growth), the same word as in mahadupacaya later in the line, fits the sense (r misread for p); also the missing space after etena

notes: The construction is loose; the genitives 'prakṛtibhedīyoktānām ... sarveṣām ... bhāvānām' are taken as the things whose being otherwise is stated, and the list in the nominative is taken with the same. mlāni = fading, withering; upacaya = growth, plumpness (alternatives possible). 'prakṛtibhedīya' is read as the section on the varieties of prakṛti; its identity is not stated in the line. 'pratiniyatānāṃbhāvānām' has a missing space.
lines_deva: एतेनम्लान्युरचयशोकहर्षरौक्ष्यस्नेहादयस्तथा प्रकृतिभेदीयोक्तानां महदुपचयसूक्ष्मदीर्घाणां सर्वेषां च दोषादिभागेन प्रतिनियतानांभावानामनिमित्ततोऽन्यथात्वमुक्तं भवति
lines_iast: etenamlānyuracayaśokaharṣaraukṣyasnehādayastathā prakṛtibhedīyoktānāṃ mahadupacayasūkṣmadīrghāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca doṣādibhāgena pratiniyatānāṃbhāvānāmanimittato'nyathātvamuktaṃ bhavati

hindi: शरीर में छायाएँ पाँच हैं।
english: As for the chāyās (shades or lustres), there are five in the body.
notes: chāyā is a technical term: shade, lustre or reflection of the body; the next units describe the five by element, so it is kept as chāyā with the general gloss 'shade, lustre'.

hindi: उनमें छपाई बिगड़ने से अस्पष्ट शब्द; स्निग्ध, मानो प्रभा सहित। वात यानी वायु से आने वाली छाया धूल और राख के समान रूखी, धूल से लाल, श्याव, प्रभाहीन और स्वेदमल की गन्ध वाली होती है।
english: Among these, unclear (damaged print: khādamlakhaṅgākāśanīlanirmalā); unctuous, as if with lustre (prabhā). From wind (vāta): dry as dust and ash, dust-reddish, dark brown, lacking lustre, smelling of sweat-waste (sveda-mala).

text_flags.why: possible: 'khādamla' is not intelligible; the pattern of lines 10 (card 9) to 13 (vātāt, tejasaḥ, aṃbhasaḥ, bhuvaḥ) calls for an ablative of the element (khāt, from ether) and amala 'stainless' fits; 'khaṅga' probably for 'khaḍga' (sword), ḍ/ṅ confusion

notes: [02.09.9] The long compound is damaged and kept unsplit; the translations say 'unclear' and the guess stays in the flag only (glossary rule). The element is ether (ākāśa), by the pattern of the next four units. 'saprabheva' = saprabhā iva. [02.09.10] The noun chāyā is understood from line 8 (card 8) (the five shades); no noun is stated here, the adjectives are feminine singular. 'pāṃśubhasmarūkṣā' is read 'dry as dust and ash'; 'rajo'ruṇā' 'reddish with dust' (rajas read as dust; no other sense is stated). The final 'gandhiḥ' is the regular feminine of the i-stem adjective -gandhi. mala here is the waste (sveda-mala, sweat-waste), not an added disease.

hindi: तेजस् यानी अग्नि से आने वाली छाया, छपाई बिगड़ने से अस्पष्ट शब्द जो रक्त यानी लाल पर समाप्त होता है, दृष्टि और मुख वाली होती है।
english: From tejas (fire): unclear (damaged print: hutahutāśavidyutasatapanīyaraktā, ending in raktā 'red'); dṛṣṭimukhā (with eye and face).

text_flags.why: possible: the letters 'asa' after vidyut are unaccounted for; the compound is read as 'red like sacrificed-to fire, lightning and gold (tapanīya)'

notes: The compound is damaged and kept unsplit; the translations say 'unclear' and the guess stays in the flag and this note (huta-hutāśa = fire fed with oblation, tapanīya = gold). 'dṛṣṭimukhā' is rendered literally 'with eye and face'; the text does not say that the colour shows in the eyes and face, though this is probable. Normalisation: tejas read as the element fire.

words.gloss: clear as vaidūrya (beryl or cat's-eye; identity disputed) and indranīla (sapphire; probable)

hindi: जल से आने वाली छाया वैदूर्य यानी लहसुनिया या बेरिल, पर पहचान विवादित है, और अनुमानित पाठ पर इन्द्रनील यानी सम्भवतः नीलम के समान निर्मल, घनी और अत्यन्त स्निग्ध होती है। पृथ्वी से आने वाली छाया सुन्दर कान्ति वाली, घनी, स्थिर, स्निग्ध, अनुमानित पाठ पर शुद्ध, श्याम और श्वेत होती है।
english: From water (ambhas): clear as vaidūrya (beryl or cat's-eye; identity disputed) and, on a conjectural reading, indranīla (probably sapphire); dense, very unctuous. From earth: of pleasing lustre, dense, steady, unctuous, on a conjectural reading pure, dusky and white.

text_flags.why: possible: 'indrīla' is not a word; 'indranīla' (sapphire) fits the pattern of gem comparisons and the letters
possible: as printed the regular sandhi reading is snigdhā + aśuddhā 'unctuous, impure', which sits oddly in a list of good qualities; 'snigdhā śuddhā' (missing space) is assumed

notes: [02.09.12] Noun chāyā understood from line 8 (card 8). vaidūrya: disputed (cat's-eye chrysoberyl or beryl); indranīla: probably sapphire (a blue gem). [02.09.13] Noun chāyā understood from line 8 (card 8). Alternative: aśuddhā 'impure' as the print stands.
lines_deva: भुवो रुचिराभा घना स्थिरा स्निग्धाशुद्धा श्यामा श्वेता च
lines_iast: bhuvo rucirābhā ghanā sthirā snigdhāśuddhā śyāmā śvetā ca

hindi: उनमें वायु वाली छाया विनाश के लिए और अत्यन्त बड़े क्लेश के लिए होती है; शेष तो सुख के उदय वाली हैं। प्रभाएँ सात हैं: रक्त यानी लाल, पीली, पाण्डुर यानी फीकी, सित यानी सफेद, असित यानी काली, श्याव यानी गहरी भूरी और हरी।
english: Of these, the one of vāyu (wind) is for destruction and for very great affliction; the remaining ones, however, are those with a rise of happiness (sukhodaya). There are seven prabhās (radiances): red, yellow, pale, white, black, dark brown and green.

text_flags.why: possible: visarga before c should become ś (haritāś ca); printed without it (the same dropped visarga before voiceless consonants occurs in raktā pītā, pītā pāṇḍurā, pāṇḍurā sitā; restored in the words as a print habit)

notes: [02.09.14] 'atimahate' is taken with kleśāya (for very great affliction); the noun is not repeated in the text. sukhodaya is literally 'rise of happiness'. [02.09.15] Final -āḥ before a voiced consonant is regular sandhi in raktā, pītā etc. asita is rendered 'black' (literally 'not white'); harita 'green' (it can also mean yellowish-green). The 'sitā 'sitā' pair is sitāḥ asitāḥ.
lines_deva: तासां वायव्या विनाशाय क्लेशाय चातिमहते शेषास्तु सुखोदयाः
सप्त प्रभा रक्ता पीता पांडुरा सिता ऽसिता श्यावा हरिता च
lines_iast: tāsāṃ vāyavyā vināśāya kleśāya cātimahate śeṣāstu sukhodayāḥ
sapta prabhā raktā pītā pāṃḍurā sitā 'sitā śyāvā haritā ca

hindi: वे स्निग्ध, विकसित होने वाली और निर्मल प्रभाएँ शुभ हैं; विपरीत तो अशुभ हैं।
english: Those (that are) unctuous, spreading and stainless are auspicious; the opposite (ones) are inauspicious.
notes: 'tāḥ' refers to the prabhās of line 15 (card 12). vikāśin is rendered 'spreading, radiant' (blooming, expanding).

hindi: उन दोनों का भेद।
english: The distinction between the two.
notes: Elliptical; the two are not named in the unit. By position they are chāyā and prabhā (lines 18 and 19 (card 15)), but this is not stated. No verb supplied.

hindi: छाया वर्ण पर छा जाती है, अनुमानित पाठ पर समीप दिखाई देती है, और पाँच भूतों से बनी है। प्रभा तो वर्ण को प्रकाशित करती है, दूर से दिखाई देती है, और तेजस् की प्रभा ही है।
english: The chāyā overspreads the colour; on a conjectural reading it is perceived as near; and it consists of the five elements (bhūta). The prabhā, however, illuminates the colour; it is perceived from afar; and it is just the radiance of tejas (fire).

text_flags.why: possible: 'calacyate' is not a word; the contrast with line 19 (card 15) (prabhā ... viprakṛṣṭā lakṣyate) suggests 'ca lakṣyate' (kṣ read as c)

notes: [02.09.18] Damaged word: 'calacyate' read as 'ca lakṣyate' on the model of line 19 (card 15); the translation marks this. ākrāmati: 'overspreads, covers'. [02.09.19] 'tejaḥprabhaiva' could also be read tejaḥ, prabhā eva ('tejas, itself prabhā'); the compound reading is used. Missing spaces in the long token.
lines_deva: प्रभा तु वर्णं प्रकाशयति विप्रकृष्टालक्ष्यतेतेजःप्रभैव च
lines_iast: prabhā tu varṇaṃ prakāśayati viprakṛṣṭālakṣyatetejaḥprabhaiva ca

words.gloss: kumārikā (little girl: probably the figure seen in the pupil)

hindi: जिसकी दृष्टि में प्रतिबिम्ब से बनी कुमारिका यानी सम्भवतः पुतली में दिखने वाली छोटी कन्या नहीं दिखाई देती, वह परासु यानी जिसके प्राण चले गए हैं।
english: He in whose eye the little girl (kumārikā, probably the small figure seen in the pupil) made of reflection is not seen is parāsu (one whose life-breath has gone).
notes: kumārikā literally 'little girl'; probable sense: the small reflected figure in the pupil (probable). dṛṣṭi is taken as 'eye' (sight). 'parāsu' literally 'whose breaths (asu) have gone away'; the verb 'is' is understood.
lines_deva: यस्य दृष्टौ प्रतिच्छायमयी कुमारिका न दृश्यते सपरासुः
lines_iast: yasya dṛṣṭau praticchāyamayī kumārikā na dṛśyate saparāsuḥ

words.gloss: in sunlight, mirror and the like

hindi: जिसकी, अनुमानित पाठ पर धूप और दर्पण आदि में, अचानक प्रतिच्छाया कटी हुई, फटी हुई, हीन, अधिक, व्याकुल, नष्ट, अनुमानित पाठ पर टेढ़ी, नीचे सिर वाली, सिरहीन, दो सिर वाली, फैली हुई, अन्य प्रकार की या विकृत दिखाई देती है।
english: He whose reflection (praticchāyā), in sunlight, on a conjectural reading mirror, and the like, is suddenly seen cut, split, deficient, in excess, confused, lost, on a conjectural reading crooked, with head downward, headless, two-headed, spread out, otherwise, or distorted.

text_flags.why: possible: ātapa + ādarśa (mirror) gives ātapādarśa; the printed form lacks one ā; 'darśa' alone does not suit the list
possible: 'jihyā' is not a word; jihmā (crooked) with h/m and y/m confusion, and a close pattern in line 28 (card 24)

notes: No predicate follows in this unit (the clause continues in the same series of conditions); the main clause is not given here. Two conjectural readings (ādarśa, jihmā) are marked in the translations. The word 'adhikā' next to 'hīnā' read as deficient / in excess. Reviewer: the printed reading ātapa-darśa-ādiṣu (on seeing sunlight etc.) is also possible; ātapādarśa (sunlight, mirror) is preferred for sense.
lines_deva: यस्यातपदर्शादिष्वकस्मात्प्रतिच्छाया छिन्ना भिन्ना हीनाऽधिकाऽऽकुला नष्टा जिह्याऽवाक्शिरा विशिरा द्विशिरा विस्तृताऽन्यथा वा विकृता वा दृश्यते
lines_iast: yasyātapadarśādiṣvakasmātpraticchāyā chinnā bhinnā hīnā'dhikā''kulā naṣṭā jihyā'vākśirā viśirā dviśirā vistṛtā'nyathā vā vikṛtā vā dṛśyate

hindi: जिसका ललाट पसीजता नहीं।
english: He whose forehead does not sweat.
notes: Relative clause only; the main clause is not in this unit.

hindi: जिसके केश और रोम तेल न लगे हुए होकर भी तेल लगे हुए के समान दिखाई देते हैं।
english: He whose head-hair and body-hair, unanointed, are seen as if anointed.
notes: One token with a missing space after yasya. abhyakta = anointed with oil or ointment.

words.gloss: of the colour of a firebrand
of abnormal colour, blue and the like

hindi: और दोनों आँखें बहुत भीतर धँसी हुई, बाहर निकली हुई, फैली हुई, सिकुड़ी हुई; सिकुड़ी भौंहों वाली, झुकी भौंहों वाली; अनुमानित पाठ पर टेढ़ी, ऊँची-नीची; रुकी हुई दृष्टि वाली, क्षीण दृष्टि वाली; नकुल यानी नेवले के समान, कपोत यानी कबूतर के समान, जलती लकड़ी के रंग की, नील आदि विकृत रंग की; बहुत चंचल, कड़ी और ढीली, बहती हुई, बहुत खुली, बहुत मिची हुई, या झड़ी पलकों वाली।
english: And the two eyes: sunk in too deep, protruding, widened, contracted; with contracted brows, with bent-down brows; on a conjectural reading crooked, uneven; with ceased sight, with deficient sight; resembling a mongoose (nakula), resembling a pigeon (kapota), of the colour of a firebrand, of abnormal colour, blue and the like; very unsteady, stiff and drooping, discharging, excessively open, excessively shut, or with lost eyelashes.

text_flags.why: possible: 'jihve' would be dual 'two tongues'; the list is of eye qualities and the neuter dual 'jihme' (crooked) fits (compare line 21, 28 (card 17/24))

notes: GROUPING: the unit has no 'yasya' and no main verb; it appears to continue the series of conditions of lines 22 and 23 (card 18/19) and to be completed in line 25 (card 21). All adjectives agree with nayane (two eyes). 'viśrānta' is kept as printed (ceased, rested); 'vibhrānta' (confused) is an alternative. nakula = mongoose (standard); the colour comparison is meant, not stated as such. 'stabdhasraste' is read as dvandva 'stiff and drooping'. Conjectural reading: jihme. Reviewer: bhruṇī (saṃkṣipta-bhruṇī, vinata-bhruṇī) is the regular neuter dual of bhru, so no emendation.
lines_deva: नयने चातिप्रविष्टे निर्गतेविस्तृते संक्षिप्ते संक्षिप्तभ्रुणी विनतभ्रुणी जिह्वे विषमे विश्रांतदर्शनेहीनदर्शने नकुलाभे कपोताभे अलातवर्णे नीलादिविकृतवर्णे अतिचले स्तब्धस्रस्ते प्रस्रुते अत्युन्मिषिते अतिनिमिषिते लुप्तपक्ष्मणीवा
lines_iast: nayane cātipraviṣṭe nirgatevistṛte saṃkṣipte saṃkṣiptabhruṇī vinatabhruṇī jihve viṣame viśrāṃtadarśanehīnadarśane nakulābhe kapotābhe alātavarṇe nīlādivikṛtavarṇe aticale stabdhasraste prasrute atyunmiṣite atinimiṣite luptapakṣmaṇīvā

words.gloss: covered with piṭikās (small boils or pustules)

hindi: या नाक बहुत खुली, बहुत बन्द, टेढ़ी, फटी हुई, पिटिका यानी छोटी फुंसियों से ढकी या सूखी, वह गतायु यानी जिसकी आयु जा चुकी है।
english: Or the nose too wide open, too closed, crooked, cracked, covered with piṭikās (small boils or pustules) or dry: he is gatāyu (one whose life-span has gone).
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete the series of conditions begun in lines 22 (card 18) to 24 (the main clause 'sa gatāyuḥ' occurs only here). The leading avagraha on 'tivivṛtā is a print habit for vā + ati. piṭikā: small boil, pustule. Reviewer: line 21 (card 17) also belongs to this series of conditions (it has no consequent either).
lines_deva: नासिका वा ऽतिविवृताऽतिसंवृता कुटिला स्फुटिता पिटिकाचिता शुष्का वा स गतायुः
lines_iast: nāsikā vā 'tivivṛtā'tisaṃvṛtā kuṭilā sphuṭitā piṭikācitā śuṣkā vā sa gatāyuḥ

words.gloss: ripe jambū fruit (Syzygium cumini, Indian blackberry; standard)

hindi: जिसका निचला होंठ नीचे जाता है और ऊपरी होंठ, या दोनों ऊपर की ओर मुख वाले, या पके जामुन यानी जम्बू फल के समान नीले।
english: He whose lower lip goes downward, and upper lip, or the two (lips) facing upward, or blue like the ripe jambū fruit (Syzygium cumini, Indian blackberry).
notes: The construction is uncertain: 'yāti' may govern both lips (lower down, upper up) and 'ūrdhvamukhau' / 'nīlau' are dual adjectives of an unstated 'two lips'. The translation keeps the uncertainty and supplies no extra verb. jambū (jāmun) = Syzygium cumini (standard).

hindi: या दाँत बहुत रूखे, ताम्र, श्याम, कीचड़ वाले, पुष्पित, कंकड़ी के कणों वाले हैं, या अचानक गिर जाते हैं।
english: Or the teeth very dry, copper-coloured, dusky, muddy, flowered, with grit (śarkarā), or they suddenly fall out.
notes: puṣpita (literally 'flowered') is kept literal; the sense (a flower-like efflorescence) is not stated. śarkarā literally 'gravel, grit, sugar'; tartar is a possible sense (not stated). The first half has no verb ('are' understood); 'patanti' belongs to the last alternative.
lines_deva: दंता वाऽतिरूक्षास्ताम्राः श्यामाः पंकिलाःपुष्पिताः सशर्करा वा सहसा वा पतंति
lines_iast: daṃtā vā'tirūkṣāstāmrāḥ śyāmāḥ paṃkilāḥpuṣpitāḥ saśarkarā vā sahasā vā pataṃti

hindi: या जीभ टेढ़ी, कड़ी, सुन्न, लिपी हुई, भारी, श्याव, सूजी हुई, सूखी, फैलने वाली, या मानो काँटों से ढकी हुई है।
english: Or the tongue crooked, stiff, numb, coated, heavy, dark brown, swollen, dry, spreading, or as if covered with thorns.

text_flags.why: possible: as printed stabdhā + asuptā would mean 'not numb'; the list of defects needs 'suptā' (missing space)

notes: 'visarpiṇī' is rendered 'spreading' only (it is not read as the disease visarpa). The 'iva vā' ending: kaṇṭaka-ācitā iva vā.
lines_deva: जिह्वा वा जिह्मा स्तब्धासुप्ताऽवलिप्ता गुर्वी श्यावा शूना शुष्का विसर्पिणी कंटकाचितेववा
lines_iast: jihvā vā jihmā stabdhāsuptā'valiptā gurvī śyāvā śūnā śuṣkā visarpiṇī kaṃṭakācitevavā

words.gloss: the attachments of cheek, forehead and jaw

hindi: जिसके गाल, ललाट और हनु यानी जबड़े के बन्धन मानो स्थान से च्युत और ढीले हैं, अनुमानित पाठ पर जिसका सिर, गर्दन या पीठ अपना भार नहीं सहता।
english: He whose attachments of cheek, forehead and jaw are slack as if fallen from their place; on a conjectural reading, whose head, neck or back does not bear its own weight.

text_flags.why: possible: 'dhante' is not a regular form; sense requires a verb 'holds, bears' (n/tt confusion)
possible: the neck as a subject (nominative) beside śiraḥ and pṛṣṭham; the final ṃ may be a print slip or may mark an accusative object
possible: printed gaṃḍe- has -e where the compound needs -a; read gaṇḍa- in the words; locative gaṇḍe is the alternative

notes: The second half is uncertain. 'yasyana' = yasya na (space missing). The reading adopted (head, neck or back does not bear its own weight, svabhāram being the object) is a conjecture; the case endings in śirodharāṃ and svabhāraṃ may point to a different construction (he does not hold up ...). Unit 30 appears to continue the sentence.
lines_deva: यस्य गंडेललाटहनुबंधनानि स्थानाच्चुतानीव स्रस्तानि यस्यन धन्ते शिरः शिरोधरां पृष्ठं वा स्वभारं
lines_iast: yasya gaṃḍelalāṭahanubaṃdhanāni sthānāccutānīva srastāni yasyana dhante śiraḥ śirodharāṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ vā svabhāraṃ

hindi: या दोनों हनु यानी जबड़े, मुख में स्थित पिण्ड।
english: Or the two jaws, a lump staying in the mouth.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue line 29 (card 25) (a verb such as 'do not hold' may be carried over, so 'the jaws ... the lump in the mouth'); no verb is supplied in the translation. Elliptical.

hindi: जिसका मेढ्र यानी पुरुष-लिंग सूजा हुआ है, या दोनों वृषण यानी अण्डकोष बहुत बाहर निकले हैं, या इससे उलटा है।
english: He whose penis (meḍhra) is swollen, or whose two testicles (vṛṣaṇa) have gone out too far, or the reverse of this.

text_flags.why: possible: the printed 'atyi' has an extra y before iniḥ; 'ati-niḥsṛtau' (very much gone out) is intended

notes: 'niḥsṛta' (gone out) is kept literal: the text does not say whether the testicles are retracted or drawn down. utsikta: swollen, raised. 'ataḥ ... viparyayaḥ' = 'the reverse of this'.
lines_deva: यस्योत्सिक्तं मेढ्रमत्यिनिःसृतौ वा वृषणावतो विपर्ययो वा
lines_iast: yasyotsiktaṃ meḍhramatyiniḥsṛtau vā vṛṣaṇāvato viparyayo vā

hindi: जिसका मूत्र बहुत उग्र है।
english: He whose urine is very fierce (strong).
notes: Relative clause only; 'ugra' (fierce) is kept general and could refer to smell or sharpness, which the text does not say.

words.gloss: one who wishes to die, about to die

hindi: जिसके विष के दोष के बिना छिद्रों से रोमकूपों सहित रक्त बहता है। जिसके अंग बिना कारण बहुत हल्के या बहुत भारी हों, वह मुमूर्षु यानी मरने की इच्छा वाला, मरने को उद्यत है।
english: He from whose orifices (kha), together with the hair-pores, blood flows out without the fault of poison. He whose limbs would be, without cause, too light or too heavy: he is mumūrṣu (one about to die; literally 'wishing to die').
notes: [02.09.33] 'prabartate' is pravartate (v/b spelling, recorded normalisation). 'viṣadoṣāt vinā' is rendered literally; the text does not name the orifices. [02.09.34] mumūrṣu is a desiderative adjective, literally 'wishing to die'; 'about to die' is the usual sense.
lines_deva: यस्य विषदोषाद्विना खेभ्यः सरोमकूपेभ्यो रक्तं प्रबर्तते
lines_iast: yasya viṣadoṣādvinā khebhyaḥ saromakūpebhyo raktaṃ prabartate

hindi: जिसका स्वर एक या अनेक, या हकलाता हुआ, अनुमानित पाठ पर अव्यक्त, कृश या दीन अचानक सुनाई देता है।
english: He whose voice, single or manifold, or stammering, indistinct (on a conjectural reading), thin or piteous, is suddenly perceived.

text_flags.why: possible: 'anyakta' is not a word; avyakta (indistinct) fits the list of voice defects (v read as n)

notes: 'ekaḥ anekaḥ' is kept literal (single or manifold). The corrected avyakta is adopted in the translations with the conjectural mark (glossary rule).
lines_deva: यस्यैकोऽनेको वा स्वरो गद्गदान्यक्तक्षामदीनो वा सहसोपलभ्यते
lines_iast: yasyaiko'neko vā svaro gadgadānyaktakṣāmadīno vā sahasopalabhyate

words.gram: desid. adj. vi+√vac, m. nom. sg.

hindi: या जो बोलना चाहता हुआ भ्रमित हो जाता है।
english: Or he who, wishing to speak, becomes bewildered.
notes: Relative clause; the main clause is not in this unit. muhyati: becomes bewildered, confused (it can also be 'faints'; the literal sense is kept).

hindi: जिसकी बोलते समय छाती ऊपर की ओर बहुत दुखती है जिसका उच्छ्वास यानी बाहर निकलती साँस बहुत लम्बी, बहुत छोटी, दुर्गन्ध वाली अथवा सुगन्ध वाली
english: He whose chest, while he speaks, aches greatly upward He whose exhalation (ucchvāsa) is too long, too short, foul-smelling or sweet-smelling
notes: [02.09.37] Part of a list of signs that is gathered up in line 43 (card 37) ('all of those are ripened by time'). 'vadataḥ' is a genitive participle, 'of one speaking'. 'ūrdhvam' is taken as an adverb, 'upward'. [02.09.38] Part of the list gathered up in line 43 (card 37). Printed 'gaṃdhi' is normalised to gandhi (orthographic, recorded once). The line has no verb; the sentence runs on.

words.gram: pass. pres. part. ā-√yam, f. nom. pl.

words.gloss: in sneezing, going, urinating and the like

hindi: जिसकी उँगलियाँ खींचे जाने पर न चटकें, और जिसका, संदिग्ध पाठ के अनुसार, 'अलग-अलग' भी शब्द छींकने, गमन, मूत्रत्याग आदि में अपनी स्वाभाविक अवस्था से परे
english: He whose fingers, when stretched, would not crack, and whose sound, even 'other and other' (reading doubtful), in sneezing, going, urinating and the like, is beyond its natural state

text_flags.why: possible: 'anyo'nyo'pi' (anyaḥ anyaḥ api) gives a poor sense; the intended word may be different (e.g. anyonyam api); no firm correction can be made, so the printed reading is kept in words

notes: Two clauses (yasya twice). 'āyamyamānā' = nom. pl. f. before voiced 'n' (āḥ drops visarga: regular). 'anyo'nyo'pi' is read literally as anyaḥ anyaḥ api; doubtful, so the translation marks it. 'gata' in kṣuta-gata-mūtraṇa is taken as 'going'; another sense (e.g. passing wind) cannot be excluded. The sentence continues; see line 43 (card 37). The Hindi 'हो' / 'चटकें' reflect the optative sphuṭeyuḥ in the first clause only.
lines_deva: यस्यांगुलय आयम्यमाना न स्फुटेयुः यस्यान्योऽन्योऽपि क्षुतगतमूत्रणादिषु स्वभावातीतः शब्दः
lines_iast: yasyāṃgulaya āyamyamānā na sphuṭeyuḥ yasyānyo'nyo'pi kṣutagatamūtraṇādiṣu svabhāvātītaḥ śabdaḥ

words.gloss: smell of garlands, fruits, sandalwood (standard), corpses and the like
in body, mouth, waste (mala), wound, clothes and the like

hindi: जिसके शरीर, मुख, मल यानी अपशिष्ट, व्रण यानी घाव, वस्त्र आदि में माला, फल, चन्दन, शव आदि की प्रिय अथवा अप्रिय गन्ध
english: He in whose body, mouth, waste (mala), wound, clothes and the like there is a smell, pleasant or unpleasant, of garlands, fruits, sandalwood, corpses and the like
notes: Part of the list gathered up in line 43 (card 37). kuṇapa = corpse (also 'carrion'). mala here is read as bodily waste (doctrinal term kept); another division of deha-mukha-mala cannot be excluded. candana = sandalwood, Santalum album (standard). The line has no verb.

hindi: जिसके शरीर को विरूपता अथवा सुरसता के कारण जूँ, मक्खी आदि बहुत छोड़ देती हैं या उसका आश्रय लेती हैं
english: He whose body, because of deformity (vairūpya) or good flavour (saurasya), lice, flies and the like greatly abandon or resort to
notes: 'atyartham' is taken with the verbs ('greatly'); it could instead qualify vairūpya/saurasya ('excessive'). The text does not say which cause goes with abandoning and which with resorting. 'yūkā' for yūkāḥ is regular sandhi; the avagraha printed in 'vā'tyartham' is a print habit (ā + a). Sentence continues; see line 43 (card 37).
lines_deva: यस्य शरीरं वैरूप्यात्सौरस्याद्वाऽत्यर्थं यूका मक्षिकादयस्त्यजंते भजंति वा
lines_iast: yasya śarīraṃ vairūpyātsaurasyādvā'tyarthaṃ yūkā makṣikādayastyajaṃte bhajaṃti vā

words.gloss: excessive coldness resembling kumuda (probably white water lily, Nymphaea, probable) and utpala (probably blue water lily, Nymphaea nouchali, probable)
in (parts) whose flesh and blood have gone

hindi: जिसके सदा गर्म रहने वाले अंगों और अवयवों में ठण्डक, अथवा ठण्डे अंगों में कुमुद यानी सम्भवतः श्वेत कुमुदिनी और उत्पल यानी सम्भवतः नीलकमल जैसी अत्यन्त शीतलता, अत्यधिक पसीना, अत्यधिक अकड़न, और जैसे मांस और रक्त चले गए हों ऐसे अंगों में ढीलापन
english: He in whom there is coldness in the limbs and parts that are constantly warm, or, in those that are (already) cold, excessive coldness resembling kumuda (probably white water lily) and utpala (probably blue water lily), excessive sweating, excessive stiffness, and slackness as if in (parts) whose flesh and blood have gone

text_flags.why: possible: 'straṃsa' is not a standard word; sraṃsa (slipping, slackness) fits the sense and the other signs

notes: Part of the list gathered up in line 43 (card 37). Identifications: kumuda = white water lily / night lotus, Nymphaea (probable); utpala = blue water lily, Nymphaea nouchali (probable); only a comparison of coldness is meant. 'sraṃsa' is kept broad (slackness, loosening). 'satatoṣmasu' read as satata-uṣman, locative plural. 'śīteṣu' taken as 'in cold (ones)' with aṅgāvayaveṣu understood. The line has no verb.
lines_deva: यस्य सततोष्मस्वंगावयवेषु शैत्यं शीतेषु वा कुमुदोत्पलानुकार्यातिशैत्यमतिस्वेदोऽतिस्तंभो विगतमांसशोणितेष्विव च स्त्रंसः
lines_iast: yasya satatoṣmasvaṃgāvayaveṣu śaityaṃ śīteṣu vā kumudotpalānukāryātiśaityamatisvedo'tistaṃbho vigatamāṃsaśoṇiteṣviva ca straṃsaḥ

hindi: और जिसके शरीर में महाभूतों का योग या अतियोग एक साथ दिखाई देता है, वे सभी कालपक्व यानी काल से पके हुए हैं
english: And he in whose body a conjunction (yoga) or excessive conjunction (atiyoga) of the great elements (mahābhūta) is seen at one time: all those are ripened by time (kālapakva)
notes: Closing 'iti' marks the end of the preceding list of signs (lines 37-43 (card 32/37)); not translated. 'yoga' is kept as literal 'conjunction'; the text does not say here what is joined, and the sense (union with, or an abnormal combination of, the elements) is not decided. 'te' (all those) refers back to the persons described in the list. 'kāla-pakva' kept literal.
lines_deva: यस्य च योगोऽतियोगो वा शरीरे युगपन्महाभूतानां दृश्यते सर्वे ते कालपक्वा इति
lines_iast: yasya ca yogo'tiyogo vā śarīre yugapanmahābhūtānāṃ dṛśyate sarve te kālapakvā iti

hindi: और इस विषय में है
english: And on this point there is
notes: Introductory formula ('bhavati cātra') that opens the verse(s) which follow; the thing that 'is' is not named in the line, so nothing is supplied.

words.gloss: at the head of the bladder (basti, bladder)

hindi: जिसकी सिराओं यानी नसों की रेखाएँ पहले कभी न देखी हुई, अथवा बालचन्द्र के समान भी ललाट पर अथवा बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय के शीर्ष पर, वह छह मास नहीं जीता
english: He whose vein-lines (sirā, vein) are unprecedented, or even like the young moon On the forehead, or at the head of the bladder (basti), he does not live six months
notes: [02.09.45] The sentence appears to be completed by the next unit (the places and the six months). 'sirā' = vein, vessel (probable; a general term for blood vessels). 'bāla-indu' = young (crescent) moon. The line has no verb. 'sirālekhā' = sirālekhāḥ (regular sandhi before voiced b). [02.09.46] Appears to complete the sentence begun in line 45 (card 39) ('whose vein-lines ...'). 'bastiśīrṣa' is kept literal ('head of the bladder'); which part is meant (upper part of the bladder, or the lower abdomen above it) is not fixed by the text. 'ṣaṇmāsān' accusative of duration, 'for six months'.

words.gloss: like a lotus leaf (padminī, lotus plant, Nelumbo nucifera, standard)

hindi: जिस देहधारी के शरीर में जल कमलिनी के पत्ते के समान तैरता है; तैरने वाले का, उसका जीवन छह मास है
english: Water, as with a lotus (padminī) leaf, in the body of whichever embodied being It floats; of one that floats, his life is six months
notes: [02.09.47] The verb appears to be in the next unit ('plavate'). Whether 'vat' compares the water's behaviour on a lotus leaf is understood but not stated, so the translation stays close to the words. [02.09.48] Appears to continue line 47 (card 40) ('water ... in the body of whichever embodied being'). 'plavamānasya' (of one floating) is difficult: it may refer to the water or to the person; the translation keeps it literal. Copula understood ('is').

hindi: जिसकी सिराएँ यानी नसें हरी-सी आभा वाली और रोमकूप बन्द वह खट्टे की इच्छा करने वाला पुरुष पित्त से मृत्यु को प्राप्त होता है
english: He whose veins (sirā) are of greenish appearance and whose hair pores are closed That man, craving the sour (amla), attains death from Pitta

text_flags.why: possible: three words printed joined without spaces (yasya, romakūpāḥ, ca); no letter changed

notes: [02.09.49] The printed 'yasyaromakūpāśca' is yasya roma-kūpāḥ ca with the space missing (a spacing matter, not a letter error). 'saṃvṛta' can mean closed or covered; 'closed' is chosen. Appears to be completed by the next unit. 'harita' = green or yellowish-green. [02.09.50] Appears to complete the sentence of line 49 (card 41). 'amla' is the sour taste. 'pittāt' is ablative, 'from/because of Pitta'. pitta is neuter.

words.gloss: up to the end of a month

hindi: जिसके सिर पर अथवा मुख पर भी गोबर के चूर्ण के समान चूर्ण अथवा सिर पर चिकनाई वाला धुआँ; उसका जीवन मास के अन्त तक है
english: He on whose head, or even on the face, there is powder resembling powder of cow dung Or smoke with oiliness on the head; his life is up to the end of a month

text_flags.why: possible: neuter nominative needs the anusvāra; the final -m seems dropped in print

notes: [02.09.51] The line has no verb; the sentence appears to run into line 52 (card 42) ('or oily smoke on the head ...'). 'mūrdhni' is the locative of mūrdhan. [02.09.52] 'vā' is read with the preceding unit's alternatives ('powder on the head ... or oily smoke on the head'); the last clause gives the life span for the signs. 'sasnehaṃ' is neuter while dhūma is masculine, so it is taken as an adverb, 'with oiliness'. 'vāmāsāṃtaṃ' = vā + māsa-antam is a reading; another division is possible. Copula understood.
lines_deva: यस्य गोमयचूर्णाभं चूर्ण मूर्ध्नि मुखेऽपि वा
सस्नेहं मूर्ध्नि धूमो वामासांतं तस्य जीवितं
lines_iast: yasya gomayacūrṇābhaṃ cūrṇa mūrdhni mukhe'pi vā
sasnehaṃ mūrdhni dhūmo vāmāsāṃtaṃ tasya jīvitaṃ

words.gloss: from six nights, after six nights
from three nights, after three nights

hindi: सिर पर अथवा दोनों भौंहों पर नए सीमन्तावर्तक यानी माँग और भँवर करते हैं स्वस्थ के लिए छह रात के बाद, किन्तु रोगी के लिए तीन रात के बाद मृत्यु
english: On the head or on the two eyebrows, new partings and whorls (sīmantāvartaka) make Death, for a healthy person after six nights, but for a sick person after three nights

text_flags.why: possible: printed 'ṣaḍarātrān' has an extra 'a' and 'n' for 't' (ta/na confusion is seen in this print); ablatives of ṣaḍrātra and trirātra fit the sense

notes: [02.09.53] GROUPING: the object of 'kurvanti' is 'mṛtyum' in line 54 (card 43), so this unit appears to continue there. 'sīmantāvartaka' is read as a dvandva 'partings and whorls' (hair-parting-like and whorl-like marks); it could also be one term for whorl-like partings, so the sense is not firm. [02.09.54] GROUPING: 'mṛtyum' is the object of 'kurvanti' in line 53 (card 43), so this unit appears to complete that sentence. The ablatives are rendered 'after' (literally 'from'); the text does not say 'within'. Which of the six or three nights counts is not stated.

hindi: जिसकी, स्नान किए और लेप लगाए हुए की, छाती पहले, बहुत सूख जाती है अनुमानित पाठ पर, सब अंगों के गीले रहते वह आधा मास नहीं जीता
english: He whose chest, when he is bathed and anointed, dries up first and greatly On a conjectural reading: while all the limbs are wet, he does not live half a month

text_flags.why: possible: 'ārdva' is not a word; ārdra (wet) fits the sense (limbs still wet while the chest is dry, line 55 (card 44)); dr/dv confusion is common in this print

notes: [02.09.55] The sentence appears to continue in line 56 (card 44) ('while all the limbs are wet ...'). 'pūrvam' = first, before the rest; 'ahead' is also possible. 'snātānuliptasya' is a genitive in the sense 'of one who has bathed and been anointed'. [02.09.56] Appears to complete line 55 (card 44). 'so'rddhamāsaṃ': 'rddh' is the print's spelling of 'rdh' (orthographic normalisation, recorded once book-wide). The locatives are read as 'with all the limbs wet'; 'ārdreṣu' stands for an unstated noun with sarvagātreṣu.

hindi: जिसकी छाती में गर्मी और जठर यानी पेट में अत्यन्त ठण्डक हो भिन्न यानी टूटा हुआ, सम्भवतः ढीला, मल और प्यास; जैसे प्रेत, वैसे ही वह
english: He in whose chest there may be heat, and in the belly (jaṭhara) excessive coldness Broken stool (bhinna; probably loose) and thirst; as a departed one (preta), just so is he

text_flags.why: possible: 'ca' printed joined to tṛṣṇā without a space; no letter changed

notes: [02.09.57] Part of a sentence that appears to run into line 58 (card 45) ('loose stool and thirst; just as a preta, so is he'). The verb 'bhavet' is stated once; 'in the belly ... excessive coldness' shares it. [02.09.58] Appears to continue line 57 (card 45). 'tṛṣṇāca' is tṛṣṇā ca with the space missing. 'bhinna purīṣa' is kept literal ('broken' stool); the modern sense (loose or watery stool) is probable but not stated. 'preta' = a departed one, a dead person. Copula understood.
lines_deva: भिन्नं पुरीषं तृष्णाच यथा प्रेतस्तथैव सः
lines_iast: bhinnaṃ purīṣaṃ tṛṣṇāca yathā pretastathaiva saḥ

hindi: मूत्र, मल, निष्ठ्यूत यानी थूक और शुक्र यानी वीर्य पानी में डूबते हैं या जिसका निष्ठ्यूत यानी थूक अनेक रंगों का हो, वह मासों में नष्ट हो जाता है
english: Urine, stool, spittle (niṣṭhyūta) and semen (śukra) sink in water Or he whose spittle (niṣṭhyūta) is of many colours perishes in months

text_flags.why: possible: 'māsān' (accusative plural) gives 'months' with no number; 'māsāt' (after a month) also fits the metre (16 syllables); the printed reading is kept in words

notes: [02.09.59] Four neuter subjects with one singular verb (taken together). 'apsu' = locative plural of ap (water), regular. The line does not say whose; the sense is of the person described in the surrounding units. niṣṭhyūta = spat-out matter, sputum. [02.09.60] The first 'vā' (or) links this to the signs of line 59 (card 46). 'māsān' is accusative plural, 'for/through months', with no number stated; the Hindi 'मासों में' is the plain rendering.
lines_deva: मूत्रं पुरीषं निष्ठ्यूतं शुक्रं चाप्सु निमज्जति
निष्ठ्यूतं बहुवर्णं वा यस्य मासान्स नश्यति
lines_iast: mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ niṣṭhyūtaṃ śukraṃ cāpsu nimajjati
niṣṭhyūtaṃ bahuvarṇaṃ vā yasya māsānsa naśyati

hindi: स्वर की दुर्बलता को और बल तथा वर्ण यानी रंग की हानि को बिना युक्ति के रोग की वृद्धि को भी देखकर मृत्यु बता दे
english: The weakening of the voice and the loss of strength and colour (varṇa) And having seen the increase of disease without reason (ayuktyā), one should foretell death
notes: [02.09.61] The object of 'dṛṣṭvā' in line 62 (card 47); the two units appear to form one sentence. 'varṇa' is colour or complexion; 'colour' is the plain rendering. [02.09.62] Appears to complete line 61 (card 47) (the signs seen are the weakening of the voice, the loss of strength and colour, and the increase of disease). 'ayuktyā' is literally 'without (proper) reason, unreasonably'; the sense might also be 'by improper means'. The agent of 'ādiśet' is not stated, so 'one'.

hindi: बिगड़े स्वर में बोलते हुए को, अपनी मृत्यु प्राप्त हुई और इसके शब्द के श्रोता को दूर से त्याग दे
english: One speaking in a faulty voice (apasvara), his own death having arrived And one should avoid from afar the hearer of his sound
notes: [02.09.63] GROUPING: lines 63 and 64 (card 48) appear to form one sentence ('parivarjayet', line 64 (card 48), probably governs the accusatives here); this is not stated as fact. The grammar of 'prāptaṃ maraṇam ātmanaḥ' is not firm: 'prāptam' may qualify the person (accusative) or agree with 'maraṇam' ('his own death having been reached'). The translation keeps the second reading. [02.09.64] GROUPING: lines 63-64 (card 48) appear to be one sentence. 'cāsyaśabdasya' is read ca + asya + śabdasya ('of this/his sound'); another division, ca + āsya-śabdasya ('of the sound of the mouth'), gives the same letters and cannot be excluded. Who is meant by 'the hearer' is not clear from the line; the translation stays literal. The agent of 'parivarjayet' is not stated ('one').

words.gloss: one whose groins are afflicted by pain

words.gram: pres. part. a-adhi-√gam, m. acc. sg.

hindi: जिसकी साँस ऊपर की ओर चढ़ती है, जिसकी गर्मी चली गई है और जिसके वंक्षण यानी जाँघ के जोड़ पीड़ा से पीड़ित हैं और सुख न पाने वाले को बुद्धिमान् त्याग दे
english: One with upward breath (ūrdhvaśvāsa), whose warmth has gone, whose groins are afflicted by pain And one finding no comfort (śarma): the intelligent one should avoid
notes: [02.09.65] Accusatives; the verb 'parivarjayet' is in line 66 (card 49), which these appear to continue into. 'ūrdhvaśvāsa' is literally 'upward breath' (a laboured, upward-rising breath; the modern term is not fixed here). 'vaṅkṣaṇa' = groin (standard). 'śūla' = pain. [02.09.66] Appears to complete line 65 (card 49) (the persons described there and here are the objects of 'parivarjayet'). The Sanskrit does not say who the intelligent one is, so none is named.

words.gloss: one in whom cold pustules have arisen
within the range of the lord of the departed (probably Yama)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, जिसके शीत पिटक यानी ठण्डी फुंसियाँ उत्पन्न हुई हैं, अथवा जिसके अंग ठण्डे हैं, वह जलता है गर्मी से द्वेष करने वाला और ठण्ड से पीड़ित, वह प्रेतों के अधिपति, सम्भवतः यम, की पहुँच में है
english: On a conjectural reading: he in whom cold pustules (piṭaka) have arisen, or who is cold-limbed, and who burns Hating heat and afflicted by cold, he is within the reach of the lord of the departed (probably Yama)

text_flags.why: possible: the printed Devanagari 'विद्ह्यते' is not a valid word; 'vidahyate' (burns, is inflamed) is a close reading and suits 'cold limbs' (inner burning with cold limbs); 'vidhyate' (is pierced) is the other possibility

notes: [02.09.67] The verb is damaged in print: the IAST 'vidhyate' (is pierced) is a valid form but the printed Devanagari is 'विद्ह्यते'; the translation adopts 'vidahyate' only on a conjectural reading, so confidence is low. 'piṭaka' = pustule, boil. 'śīta-piṭaka' read as 'cold pustules' (the text gives no further detail). The sentence appears to run on into line 68 (card 50). [02.09.68] Appears to complete line 67 (card 50). 'pretādhipa' = lord of the departed; Yama is the usual identification (probable). 'gocara' = range, domain. Copula understood ('he is').

hindi: जिसके कण्ठ पर रस्सी जैसी छाया लगी हुई दिखाई देती है वह प्राणी निश्चय ही शीघ्र यम के सेवकों द्वारा खींच लिया जाता है
english: He on whose neck a shadow like a rope is seen attached That living being is surely dragged away soon by the servants of Yama
notes: [02.09.69] The sentence appears to be completed in line 70 (card 51) (he is dragged by Yama's servants). 'chāyā' = shadow (also 'lustre'); 'shadow' is the plain rendering. [02.09.70] Appears to complete line 69 (card 51). 'kṛṣyate' is a passive, 'is dragged' (pulled).

words.gloss: concerned with knowing abnormal limbs (name of the chapter)

hindi: इस प्रकार विकृताङ्गविज्ञानीय नामक नवम अध्याय
english: Thus the ninth chapter, named Vikṛtāṅgavijñānīya
notes: Colophon. 'vikṛtāṅgavijñānīya' is kept as the chapter's name; it is formed from vikṛta (abnormal), aṅga (limb or part) and vijñānīya (concerning knowledge). The leading '||' is kept as a token.
